I’ve been struggling with a pretty fixed mindset about habits and personal change. Part of me believes that the habits we develop or fail to develop during childhood become so deeply ingrained that changing them later is extremely difficult.

For example, when I notice myself repeatedly falling back into the same routines, procrastinating, or having trouble staying consistent with something I genuinely want to improve, I start thinking, “Maybe this is just how I am.” That thought makes it even harder to try again because I begin expecting myself to eventually fall back into my old patterns.

What I’m trying to understand is whether people can actually make lasting changes to habits they’ve had for years. I’m especially interested in hearing from people who once considered themselves undisciplined, inconsistent, or stuck in their ways but gradually became different.

Was there a specific moment when things changed for you, or was it a slow process? What habits did you change, and how long did it take before the new behavior started feeling normal? Did you have periods where you slipped back into your old habits, and if so, what helped you continue instead of deciding that you had failed?

I’m not really looking for a quick motivational quote or a “just be disciplined” answer. I’d love to hear actual experiences, including changes that seemed small at first. I think hearing concrete examples from people who have changed would help challenge my belief that our childhood habits permanently determine who we become.
